headline: Acquisition lifts sales and margins, outlook reaffirmed
summary_short: Net sales rose 17.4% y/y to $2,024.8M, with 14.6 points from the McCormick de Mexico acquisition and 1.9% organic growth. Adjusted EPS was $0.86 versus $0.85; GAAP EPS fell to $0.36 on special charges.
summary_long: Sales growth was mostly acquisition-driven (McCormick de Mexico), with organic growth of 1.9% led by price. Gross margin expanded 190bp on the acquisition, higher sales and cost savings, partly offset by commodity and freight costs. GAAP operating income fell on $141.5M of special charges, including transaction and integration costs and a non-cash impairment. Fiscal 2026 outlook reaffirmed: adjusted EPS $3.05 to $3.13. Cash was $331.1M; Unilever Foods combination expected to close by mid-2027.
confidence_notes: Adjusted figures are management non-GAAP measures. GAAP operating income and EPS include special charges (EPS impact $0.50). Prior-year comparisons are affected by the January 2026 consolidation of McCormick de Mexico. q/q net sales delta uses the prior-quarter shard value.

drivers.explanation: McCormick de Mexico contributed 14% to the sales increase; organic sales rose 2%, driven by price, and currency added 1%.
Driven by the McCormick de Mexico acquisition, higher sales and CCI cost savings, partially offset by higher commodity and freight costs.
Special charges of $141.5M, including transaction and integration costs and a non-cash impairment of a Malaysia pepper sourcing project, weighed on GAAP results.
Higher gross profit and CCI cost savings including SG&A streamlining, partly offset by higher SG&A from acquisition, brand marketing and technology investments.
Higher adjusted operating income, partially offset by a higher tax rate and higher interest expense.
Management cites productivity initiatives offsetting rising input and freight costs, supporting margin expansion and continued brand investment.
